title: Red Shift and the Expanding Universe - Check 1

questions.stem: What happens to the wavelength of light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?
questions.explanation: When a galaxy moves away from us, the light it emits is stretched to longer wavelengths, shifting it towards the red end of the spectrum. This is known as red shift and is a consequence of the Doppler effect applied to light.

questions.stem: Hubble's law states that the recessional velocity of a galaxy is:

options.text: Inversely proportional to its distance from us
Directly proportional to its distance from us
Equal for all galaxies regardless of distance
Proportional to the square of its distance from us

questions.explanation: Hubble's law (v = H₀d) states that a galaxy's recessional velocity is directly proportional to its distance from us. This means that more distant galaxies are moving away faster, which is key evidence for the expansion of the universe.
